title: Formal binary Morse normalization with invertible polar matrix
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $S=F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$. Let $f\in\mathfrak p^2$ have homogeneous degree-two part $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$, where $a,b,c\in F$ and $b^2-4ac\ne0$. Then there exists a continuous $F$-algebra automorphism $\alpha:S\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ with $\alpha(u)-u,\alpha(v)-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and $\alpha(f)=Q$. Continuity is for the $\mathfrak p$-adic topology (the powers $\mathfrak p^N$ form a basis of neighbourhoods of zero). No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), successive corrections using the invertible polar matrix; the same correction calculation applied to a single power series before passing to its quotient.

proof.text: Start with $x_2=u$, $y_2=v$. The hypothesis on the quadratic part gives $f-Q(x_2,y_2)\in\mathfrak p^3$. Inductively, suppose $x_r-u,y_r-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and $f-Q(x_r,y_r)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ for $r\ge2$. Apply [lem-trf-binary-quadratic-order-correction] with this same fixed $f$ and these $x_r,y_r$. Choose its outputs as $x_{r+1},y_{r+1}$; they preserve tangency, have increments in $\mathfrak p^r$, and satisfy $f-Q(x_{r+1},y_{r+1})\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. This recursion gives the two sequences with all these bounds.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), successive corrections and completeness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-binary-quadratic-successive-limit] to these sequences: the initial pair is $(u,v)$, and step 1 gives each increment in $\mathfrak p^r$ for $r\ge2$. It gives limiting coordinates $x_\infty-u,y_\infty-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and an $F$-algebra automorphism $\beta$ with $\beta(u)=x_\infty$, $\beta(v)=y_\infty$. Both $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$ are continuous and preserve every $\mathfrak p^N$. Apply its final assertion with the same coefficients $a,b,c$ and fixed series $f$: the error bounds of step 1 hold for every $r\ge2$, so $f=Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)=\beta(Q)$.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), successive corrections and completeness.

proof.text: Put $\alpha=\beta^{-1}$. It is continuous and preserves $\mathfrak p^2$ by step 2. Applying $\alpha$ to $\beta(u)-u\in\mathfrak p^2$ gives $u-\alpha(u)\in\mathfrak p^2$; negating gives the required tangent condition, and likewise for $v$. Applying it to $f=\beta(Q)$ yields $\alpha(f)=Q$. The two cited lemmas impose no characteristic restriction beyond the given discriminant condition.

Q(x',y') − Q(x,y) = L1A + L2B + Q(A,B), with L_i(x,y) − L_i ∈ p², A(x,y) − A(u,v) ∈ p^{r+1} and Q(A,B) ∈ p^{2r} ⊆ p^{r+2} for r≥2, so f − Q(x',y') ∈ p^{r+2} in every characteristic. The quadratic congruence holds for any a,b,c, and ∩p^{r+1}=0 gives f=β(Q).
